exposure: Patients grouped by decade of delivery (2001-2010 vs. 2011-2021)
cohort: 195 patients who underwent obstetric hysterectomy (OH) out of 19,666 total deliveries at a rural tertiary care referral center in western India over a 20-year period (2001-2021)
finding: While the overall incidence of obstetric hysterectomy (OH) remained stable, the study found a significant shift in indications for OH, with a decrease in uterine rupture and an increase in morbidly adherent placenta.
mod_finding: Although the incidence of OH in cesarean deliveries increased, this was attributed to the overall rise in cesarean section rates.
